introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Citizenship Education 2 (0562), Paper 2, ORDINARY INTERMEDIATE LEVELS, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates:

- You are required to answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B, and C.
- All the questions carry equal marks and marks allocated to different parts of questions are indicated.
- Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Regles de choix : la page de garde dit « answer FOUR questions choosing QUESTION 1 and THREE others from Sections A, B, and C ... Extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked ». Le sujet a 3 sections (A : questions 2, 3, 4 ; B : questions 5, 6, 7 ; C : questions 8, 9, 10). `regles_choix` contient une regle `parmi 1 sur 3` par section (lecture retenue : une question par section, les questions en trop d'une section n'etant pas corrigees) ; la question 1 est obligatoire (`groupes` COMPULSORY, aucune regle). La phrase « three others from Sections A, B and C » n'indique pas explicitement « une par section » : c'est une lecture, appuyee sur « extra question(s) answered from each section shall NOT be marked ».

Page de garde verifiee : « 0562 CITIZENSHIP EDUCATION 2 », JUNE 2020, « ORDINARY INTERMEDIATE LEVELS » (niveau Ordinary), Paper 2, code 0562, deux heures et demie. Sujet avec une couche texte tres bruitee (caracteres parasites) : toutes les pages ont ete lues en image. Filigrane gcerevision.com / Kawlo sans incidence sur la lecture.

Points : la page de garde dit « all the questions carry equal marks » et le sujet imprime un seul total entre parentheses par question ou par sous-question (Q1 : 1+1+2+1 / 1+2+1 / 2+1+2 / 2+4 ; Q2 : 6+8+6 ; Q3 : 3+6+6+5 ; Q4 : 7+7+6 ; Q5 : 7+8+5 ; Q6 : 3+10+7 ; Q7 : 6+7+7 ; Q8 : 4+10+6 ; Q9 : 10+5+5 ; Q10 : 6+7+7). Chaque question vaut donc 20 (`points` de l'exercice = 20, somme des barèmes imprimés, aucun point modifie). Quand le sujet imprime des nombres qui ne correspondent pas un a un aux sous-questions, la repartition par sous-question est de notre fait : Q3 b = 6 + 6 (causes, consequences), Q7 a = 3 + 3, Q8 a = 2 + 2, Q9 b = 5 + 5 (Gouvernement, communaute internationale), Q10 a = 3 + 3 et b = 7 + 7.

Aucun corrige officiel : les corriges sont des reponses modeles redigees sans source consultable. Les faits cites (institutions, textes, evolution constitutionnelle) sont formules de maniere generale et prudente, sans numero d'article de loi autre que ceux imprimes dans le sujet, et sont a faire relire par un enseignant d'education civique avant toute mise en avant.

Q10(b) : « any one of the above » : le corrige developpe le travail des enfants (causes et consequences) et ajoute un court modele pour la traite ; un candidat n'en traite qu'un. Le sujet imprime « (6 +7+7 marks) » ; a = 6 (3 + 3), b = 7 + 7 = 14 (de notre fait).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Define:

(i) Child Labour.

(ii) Child Trafficking.

[6 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Child labour** is the **employment of children in work that is harmful to their health, safety, education or development**, or that is too heavy for their age, so that it takes away their childhood and their schooling.

**(ii) Child trafficking** is the **recruitment, transport, transfer, hiding or receiving of a child for exploitation** (forced labour, begging, domestic work, sexual exploitation), inside the country or across borders, with or without the child's consent.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Explain the causes and consequences of any one of the above.

[7 + 7 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(The candidate chooses ONE of child labour or child trafficking. The model answer below treats **child labour**; a short model for child trafficking follows.)*

**Child labour: causes (7 marks)**

1. **Poverty**: poor families send children to work or sell goods to add to the family income.
2. **Ignorance** of the value of education and of children's rights by some parents.
3. **Large families** and lack of means to pay school fees.
4. **Death or illness of parents** (including HIV/AIDS), which leaves orphans to care for themselves.
5. **Demand for cheap labour**: employers prefer children because they are cheap and obedient.
6. **Weak enforcement of laws** and lack of control by the authorities.
7. **Cultural beliefs** that children must work early, and **rural poverty** and school dropout.

**Child labour: consequences (7 marks)**

1. **Poor health**: injuries, illness and tiredness.
2. **School dropout and illiteracy**, which closes the way to better jobs.
3. **Physical and psychological abuse**: violence, insults and loss of self-confidence.
4. **Loss of childhood**: no play, rest or family care.
5. **Perpetual poverty**: uneducated children grow into poor adults, so poverty continues from one generation to the next.
6. **Delinquency and bad habits**: drug use, theft and prostitution in the street.
7. **A less skilled workforce for the country**, and bad image of the country abroad.

**Alternative: child trafficking (short model).** *Causes:* poverty, the promise of schooling or work abroad, organised criminal networks, weak border controls and weak law enforcement, ignorance of parents. *Consequences:* physical and sexual abuse, psychological trauma, loss of family and education, spread of diseases including HIV/AIDS, and an increase in crime and in the cost of fighting it.
